title: U.S. News/NIPNLG: 26 ICE Detention Deaths Through 7 Months of 2026, On Pace for All-Time Record
excerpt: Tracking data published by U.S. News and NIPNLG confirmed 26 reported ICE custody deaths through the first seven months of 2026—on pace to exceed last year's record of 33 by more than 25%. Delaney Hall in Newark alone had seen three deaths from medical emergencies, while the facility was documented to have contaminated food, extreme temperatures, and overcrowding.
content:
Reporting by U.S. News and tracking by the National Immigration Project (NIPNLG) confirmed that at least 26 people had died in ICE custody through the first seven months of 2026—placing the year on pace to exceed 2025's record-high 33 deaths by more than 25%.

The rapid rise in deaths coincides with the Trump administration's expansion of ICE detention to over 68,000 detainees in February 2026, an increase of roughly 70% from the Biden administration. A JAMA study published in April found the ICE detention mortality rate had hit a 22-year high in the opening months of FY2026.

  • 2025 saw 33 deaths in ICE custody—the highest annual total in more than two decades, eclipsing deaths in the prior four years combined.
  • ICE simultaneously reduced the information it makes public about detainee deaths, and separately eliminated the rule requiring reporting of deaths occurring after release from custody (June 2026).
  • Delaney Hall in Newark was responsible for at least three deaths after medical emergencies; state health inspectors had been repeatedly denied entry to the facility.
  • Priciliano Trejo, 29, died July 24, 2026 at Stewart Detention Center after his family reported he was not receiving medical care for leukemia; Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, 41, died August 1, 2026 at Delaney Hall after a medical emergency.
